Chapter Five: The Strangeness and Power of the Christian Story.
You know, there’s a real tendency these days to treat Christianity as something ordinary—just another entry in the long list of world religions. But if you really stop and pay attention, the story itself is anything but ordinary. It’s strange. It’s unsettling. And, honestly, it’s incredibly powerful.
Think about someone who’s grown up hearing the story of Jesus so many times, it just fades into the background. The words are familiar, the rituals become routine. But sometimes, out of nowhere, something cuts through—a single line in a song, a moment of silence, or a sudden realization. And in that moment, it clicks: this story isn’t just about a wise teacher or a tragic figure. No, it’s about a God who actually becomes human, who suffers, dies, and then rises again.
That’s not the kind of story people just make up. It’s too surprising, too challenging, and honestly, it’s full of paradox.
The Christian story is packed with surprises. The hero isn’t born into power or privilege, but in poverty. The big victory? It comes through what looks like defeat. And the greatest command isn’t about strength or conquest—it’s to love, even when it costs you everything. The message isn’t about escaping this world, it’s about redeeming it. And it’s not about earning favor, but receiving grace.
Here’s something to pay attention to: this very strangeness is actually the story’s strength. It’s what keeps the story alive, no matter how many times people try to simplify or explain it away. It challenges us to see ourselves—and the world—in a whole new light. It offers hope, not by pretending suffering doesn’t exist, but by transforming it.
Over the years, people have tried to make Christianity more reasonable, more respectable, more like everything else. But at its core, the story just refuses to be tamed. It insists on the impossible—that the world isn’t what it seems, that love really is the final word.
And for anyone willing to really listen, the story still carries just as much power as ever. It speaks to the deepest longings of the human heart—the need for meaning, for forgiveness, for hope. It’s an invitation to step into a different reality, to believe that the ordinary can actually become extraordinary, and that even death can give way to life.
